fields.sections.2.h: Benchmark Performance in Computer Operation Capability
fields.sections.3.h: Visual Reasoning and Desktop Automation Performance
fields.sections.4.h: Tangible Progress in Reducing Hallucinations and Errors
fields.sections.5.h: Significant Enhancement in Software Engineering Capability
fields.sections.0.ko: OpenAI unveiled GPT-6.1 Terra, a fast, low-cost model combining visual reasoning and computer operation capability. It shows significant improvement over the previous generation GPT-5.6 Terra and handles practical tasks well such as proposal writing, technical drawing interpretation, form filling, and video editing. The model is designed beyond simple performance improvement, aiming to automate communication and computer work that users face daily.
fields.sections.1.ko: Terra's API pricing is 50% cheaper compared to GPT-5.6 Terra and GPT-6.1 Sol, making it practical for automating large volumes of repetitive tasks (e.g., invoice reading and accounting software input). In ChatGPT Work and Codex plans, it is designed to handle significantly more work than previous models with the same usage quota. This represents OpenAI's strategy to establish a new standard for cost-to-intelligence across the entire model family.
fields.sections.2.ko: In OpenAI's measurement on Agents' Last Exam, a specialized task benchmark, Terra achieved a score 15 points higher than GPT-5.6 Terra at intermediate reasoning level at approximately one-third of the cost. Remarkably, it shows comparable performance to GPT-6 Astra while costing only one-tenth per token. At maximum reasoning level, it has token efficiency 3 times or greater than Claude Opus 5.5 and costs one-quarter of the price, resulting in total cost per task approximately 9 times lower. Additionally, task completion speed is more than 3 times faster than both GPT-6 Astra and GPT-6.1 Sol.
fields.sections.3.ko: In the MMMU-Pro visual reasoning benchmark, Terra surpasses GPT-5.6 Terra across all reasoning settings and achieves nearly equivalent performance to top-performing models GPT-6 Astra and GPT-6.1 Sol at significantly lower cost. In the OSWorld 2.1 test (measuring the ability to complete multi-step tasks using desktop apps), it exceeds the previous generation's top score at intermediate reasoning level while cost per task is a fraction.
fields.sections.4.ko: OpenAI invested heavily this year in reducing hallucinations and factual errors in the model. In internal benchmarks, the error rate at low reasoning level plummeted 37 points from 53.6% in GPT-5.6 Terra to 16.7% in GPT-6.1 Terra. At maximum reasoning level, the error rate also declined 18 points, reaching 4.3%, approaching the level of GPT-6 Astra and GPT-6.1 Sol.
fields.sections.5.ko: In the Terminal-Bench 4.0 test (measuring coding problem-solving capability on the command line), Terra at maximum reasoning level achieved a 50.3% resolution rate, more than double the 21.5% of the previous generation. However, for the most complex coding tasks, GPT-6.1 Sol and GPT-6 Astra remain better choices. In the Terminal-Bench-Science 0.1 test (measuring the ability to apply code to scientific research tasks), Terra surpasses GPT-6.1 Sol while achieving performance within 5 points of Opus 5.5 at less than one-fifth of the cost.
fields.sections.6.ko: OpenAI continues to train and refine safety mechanisms while making powerful AI more efficient and accessible. Terra meets the highest threat level (Critical) in the cybersecurity sector within the readiness framework and maintains protection features developed for GPT-6 Astra. Inheriting alignment improvements from the GPT-6 series, Terra tends to not go out of scope and honestly disclose limitations and potential obstacles more strongly than GPT-5.6 Terra. It also demonstrates strong resistance to prompt injection attacks.
fields.sections.7.ko: GPT-6.1 Terra is immediately available to all Plus, Pro, Enterprise, and Edu users of ChatGPT Work and Codex, and developers can access it via OpenAI API as 'gpt-6.1-terra'. API pricing is $1 per million input tokens, $0.05 per million cached input tokens, and $5 per million output tokens.
fields.caveat: All benchmark figures are OpenAI's internal measurements released without independent verification, so actual performance in working environments may vary depending on use cases.
